name: The Prediction Error Encoding Principle
short_description: Prediction error is the master mechanism of learning: every effective instructional method works by generating PE (testing, generation, interleaving, active learning); passive methods fail because they generate no PE
higher_order_principle: PREDICTION ERROR IS THE MASTER MECHANISM OF LEARNING. Every effective instructional method works by generating prediction errors that enhance hippocampal encoding. Every ineffective method fails because it generates no prediction errors. Testing (forces prediction → often wrong → PE), generation (produces candidate answer → often wrong → PE), interleaving (disrupts category-based prediction → PE), active learning (requires prediction → frequent PE), elaborative interrogation (asks 'why?' → forces causal prediction → PE when wrong). Passive methods (rereading, highlighting, listening) generate no predictions and therefore no PE and therefore no encoding signal.

unifying_principle.claim: All effective learning methods share the common mechanism of generating prediction errors
unifying_principle.passive_methods_fail_because: they generate no predictions and therefore no PE
unifying_principle.active_methods_succeed_because: they force predictions that are often wrong, generating PE

causal_links.evidence_base: Roediger & Karpicke, 2006; Bjork & Bjork, 2011; Freeman et al., 2014

high_PE_methods.testing_retrieval_practice: student generates prediction (answer) → compared to correct answer → PE drives encoding [d = 0.5-0.7 vs. restudy]
high_PE_methods.generation: student produces answer BEFORE being told → even wrong generation enhances subsequent encoding [Richland et al., 2009]
high_PE_methods.interleaving: mixing categories disrupts category-level predictions → forces discriminative processing [d = 0.4 vs. blocking]
high_PE_methods.active_learning: student makes predictions, tests them against reality → frequent PE [d = 0.5 vs. lecture, Freeman et al., 2014]
high_PE_methods.Socratic_questioning: teacher asks questions that expose misconceptions → student's implicit prediction is wrong → PE

low_PE_methods.rereading: material matches what was read before → PE = 0 → minimal encoding
low_PE_methods.passive_lecture: student receives information without generating predictions → PE = 0
low_PE_methods.note_copying: transcription without comprehension → no semantic prediction → PE = 0

causal_links.evidence_base: Davachi, 2006; Kumaran & Maguire, 2006; Greve et al., 2017

parameters.mechanism: CA1 mismatch detection → encoding signal → enhanced LTP → stronger trace
parameters.connects_to: ED1 (hippocampal encoding) — PE is the primary driver; T1 (prediction error) — same fundamental mechanism

causal_links.evidence_base: implied by Bjork desirable difficulty framework; Metcalfe hypercorrection

parameters.inverted_U_possibility: Very large PE (incomprehensible material) may NOT enhance encoding because error is too large to resolve. Moderate PE (surprising but comprehensible) may be optimal.
parameters.Metcalfe_hypercorrection: High-confidence errors produce largest PE when corrected → produce BEST learning. Confidence × error = large PE → large encoding enhancement.

scope_conditions: PE requires that a PREDICTION was generated — if learner is not engaged enough to predict, no PE occurs
PE must be RESOLVABLE — incomprehensible PE produces confusion, not learning
Social/emotional context modulates: PE as threat activates amygdala stress; PE in safe context activates hippocampal encoding

This principle unifies Bjork's desirable difficulties, Roediger's testing effect, Karpicke's retrieval-based learning, Freeman's active learning, and van Kesteren's schema-violation encoding under a SINGLE mechanism
moderators: prediction_generation (learner must actually make a prediction)
PE_resolvability (moderate PE optimal; too large is unresolvable)
confidence_level (high-confidence errors produce largest learning gains when corrected)
social_emotional_context (safe context enables encoding; threat context blocks it)

goldilocks_zone.too_little_PE: material too easy, too familiar, passively delivered → no encoding signal → no learning
goldilocks_zone.optimal_PE: material surprising but comprehensible, active prediction, moderate difficulty → strong encoding → deep learning
goldilocks_zone.too_much_PE: material incomprehensible, unrelated to schemas, overwhelming → unresolvable PE → confusion, frustration

interactions.nature: ED6 applies the general prediction error mechanism (T1) specifically to learning and memory encoding.
PE (ED6) is the primary driver of hippocampal encoding (ED1).
Testing effect (ED3) is one specific manifestation of the PE encoding principle (ED6).
Schema violation (ED4) is a high-level form of PE (ED6) that drives strong encoding.

ecological_testability: HIGH — PE operationally defined as discrepancy between student's prediction/answer and correct answer. Measurable in any classroom by having students predict before being told.
